## Actionable non-OK findings

1. **.1.9 — preserve the closure dispute.** Comment 73 is explicit and remains the final comment on this assigned record. Later .1.12/.1.11 evidence is relevant to reconciliation, but do not erase the dispute or pretend the original six schema checks proved semantic coverage. Main should append a source-bound disposition of comments 66/68/73 and reconcile the close reason.
2. **.1.5 — reconcile the effective-policy receipt contract.** The record explicitly assigns the generic runtime seam to .5.1/.5.11 and tests to .5.19/.5.20, so this is not evidence of a wholly ownerless product obligation. The defect is the closed P0 record’s unqualified receipt/revalidation AC versus its narrower closure evidence. Record what P0 froze and what P4 still must implement; do not require later P6/P7/P8 commands to close P0.
3. **.2.4 — attach closure provenance.** The recorded 8/8 assertion is evidence that tests were reported, not the exact source/command/artifact binding required by its AC. Record the endpoint implementation revision and scoped execution evidence, with the redirect and credential-routing coverage distinguished from later transport integration.
4. **Root epic — correct current-tense unstarted status.** The body contradicts its own implementation-started notes. Historical tracker-conversion comments can remain unchanged.
5. **Expected pending proof, not defects:** .1, .2, .2.2, .2.3, .2.5, .2.6, .2.7, .2.8, .2.9, .2.10, .2.11, .2.12. Their individual missing evidence is enumerated above.

## Recent correction and reference reconciliation

- The archived review located the named recent commits in the recorded Git history. No fresh Git command or source audit was run here.
- 02c08a3 addresses the nonexistent-reference rejection defect; the recorded review explicitly limits that result to source-reference validation, not exhaustive semantic coverage or execution of every referenced test.
- .1.12 comment 105 explicitly binds the overwritten-unittest-method correction to 44722c3 and supersedes its earlier nothing-to-commit wording. Do not report that correction as unpublished.
- .1.11 comment 107 explicitly includes 44722c3, 9cfef79 and adapter c80949c in the candidate based on 92553e3; its final close reason records the subsequent accepted implementation and acceptance commits. Its earlier “acceptance remains open” progress comment is historical, not by itself a contradiction of final closure.
- The nonexistent tests/contract_matrix_contract.rs reference is recorded as an earlier defect in .1.9, not a newly verified current missing file. Do not turn that historical report into a fresh source claim.
- No new broken-reference or ownerless-obligation finding is established by the assigned records. References to later-phase owners are handoffs, not proof that those owners have completed their work.

## Four peer-added records: duplication versus gaps

All four are justified corrective work items within existing roadmap obligations, not evidence that four original product capabilities were missing from the roadmap:

- sr-7dvc: concrete privacy regression inside .1.5’s unknown-key/config diagnostic contract.
- sr-8d2m: concrete construction-path regression inside .1.4’s nonzero bounded-runtime contract.
- sr-adapter-audit-3djt: concrete defects inside .1.6’s pure adapter/capability contract, with aggregate P0 acceptance separately owned.
- sr-adapter-followup-s3n0: additional direct-call invariant and explicit-source defects after that audit; it preserves the P3 integration boundary and explicitly hands off the separate caller problem.

Their overlap is intentional defect ownership, not grounds to merge them into another fresh implementation track or delete their pre-fix evidence.

## P1 contract-completeness conclusion

The assigned protocol records collectively specify the endpoint, credentials, deadlines, request/response bounds, retry admission and evidence separation coherently: trusted HTTPS base origin joined once to /v1/systemone; no URL credentials; credential-free loopback exception; origin-scoped bearer routing; explicit proxy policy; redirects/internal retries disabled; entry deadline propagated through all effects with cleanup reserve; every retry freshly admitted and charged; unknown usage never zero; separate bounded batch policy; and live proof distinct from local fixtures. No additional protocol-obligation GAP is established by these records. The remaining work is the recorded execution/acceptance proof, particularly .2.4’s closure provenance.

## Verification boundary

This is a read-only acceptance review. The suggested fresh runtime command would violate the assignment’s explicit prohibition on validation commands and provider calls, and is unnecessary to identify these tracker defects. No runtime behavior was freshly verified; all test totals above are attributed to recorded evidence. Main owns all tracker amendments and any project-wide validation.

## Amendments warranted

1. **sr-roadmap-l1i.5.16 — CONTRADICTION.** Its embedded I05 onboarding contract requires README to identify the “present documentation-only status before its command examples and installation instructions.” AGENTS.md:59–62 explicitly requires the requested finished-product voice and says not to add a design-stage banner; the comprehensive plan's opening alignment paragraph agrees. The same obsolete sentence remains in the plan's I05 paragraph, so this is conflicting governing prose inherited by the bead, not evidence that the demo implementation failed. Preserve honest technical status in capability/engineering/evidence records without ordering a forbidden README banner.
2. **sr-roadmap-l1i.5.17 — CONTRADICTION.** Its embedded I05 paragraph repeats the same documentation-only README requirement, conflicting with the current finished-product instruction. Doctor's separation of key presence, network consent, historical transport checks and optional ledger readiness is otherwise consistent. Correct the inherited documentation instruction; leave product ACs open pending proof.

## Targeted consistency findings

- **Namespace:** .5/.5.7/.5.8/.5.10/.5.11/.5.20 agree on workspace/session/agent-branch namespaces, context epoch, adapter/schema/visibility and key generation. Request fingerprints are separate from decisions and delivery identities. Identical redacted text is not cross-session sharing authority. .6.9/.6.10 explicitly prevent cass or normalized producers from advancing native observation cursors merely by matching paths/session IDs.
- **TTL versus observation versus retention:** response validity is 10 minutes from provider receipt, never renewed by reads/copies; negative ages/future timestamps invalidate. Observation attribution ends at the earliest next prompt/task boundary/session end/30 minutes. Ledger logical retention is 30 days. These are different clocks with consistent uses, not competing TTLs.
- **Stage compatibility:** changing M, lowering a gate into an uncaptured stage, changed shortlist/request inputs, or incompatible model evidence cannot silently reuse another stage. Unversioned aliases prohibit cached-wide/fresh-rerank mixing. Replay freezes time/policy/eligibility and cannot import results into the live cache.
- **Attribution/accounting:** shared responses do not share event IDs, decisions, exposures or judgments. Owners alone incur new attempt/usage counts; followers/cache consumers report zero new usage and retain provenance. Missing owner accounting remains unknown. Generated/prepared/emitted/acknowledged states are distinct; empty shadow output is not exposure. Latest preceding same-agent/turn emission wins attribution only with a proven boundary, and observations/loaded state/cursor CAS commit together.
- **Persistence:** no-cache, no-ledger, no-persist and dry-run remain independent restrictive controls. Ordinary configuration/input reads remain permitted under no-persist; replay is intentionally stricter. Optional cache/ledger failure cannot silently reset protected allowance accounting. Clear fences old writers but permits new-generation recording. Quotas include maintenance reserve, sidecars/backups/temp, with no secure-erasure claim.
- **Calibration/evaluation:** P5 supplies loss/metric/sampling machinery; references to calibration and priors do not authorize enabling P8 adaptation early. Loss 0/1/2, common judged cohorts, incomplete-versus-failed-versus-unstarted cases, fixed family splits, diagnostic seeds, weighted means and independent harm cohorts are consistently distinguished. .6.23 explicitly assigns optional pilot allocation to .10.14 rather than blocking P5.
- **Minor historical-comment drift, not a closure defect:** .6 parent comment 11 lists the old .6.23 title “Separate diagnostic review queues and evaluate pilot allocation.” The current assigned .6.23 record clearly limits P5 to diagnostic queues and supplies the later owner. Prefer the current scoped record; the old handoff title is not a missing owner or proof of completion.

## Reference checks

- `scripts/e2e/run.sh`, `tests/contract_matrix.toml`, and `.env.example` exist.
- Referenced external source paths exist: frankenscipy `crates/fsci-stats/src/lib.rs`; franken_numpy `crates/fnp-random/src/lib.rs`; frankenpandas `crates/fp-join/src/lib.rs` and `crates/fp-frame/src/lib.rs`. Only existence was checked; no backend source audit or qualification was performed.

## Amendments warranted

The same stale I05 sentence appears in sr-roadmap-l1i.7 (line 186), sr-roadmap-l1i.7.9 (line 61), and sr-roadmap-l1i.8.5 (line 92): 'The README must identify the present documentation-only status before its command examples and installation instructions.' Prefer foundation/bootstrap-only status with planned command examples and unavailable product workflows explicitly distinguished. This is a narrow wording correction, not a reason to close any product bead; all three also still require their scoped acceptance evidence.

## Requested acceptance findings

### Experimental-before-promotion: retained in AC text

- sr-roadmap-l1i.8.9 ACs enable only explicit scoped trusted experimental selection while keeping ordinary shadow defaults and public readiness unchanged. Independent actual-harness acceptance belongs to the separate trial gate.
- sr-roadmap-l1i.8.10 ACs require real supported-harness default silence plus a valid experimental emission, outage rollback and truthful delivery evidence. It explicitly accepts a mechanism, not quality or production readiness.
- sr-roadmap-l1i.8.3, .8.4 and .8.5 each have a specific final AC requiring the independently verified experimental delivery path for advisory outcomes. Their embedded prerequisite names .8.9/.8.10 and expressly says not to wait for or prematurely claim .8.6 public promotion.
- sr-roadmap-l1i.8.6's final AC requires original complete relevance, harm, operational and trial studies; experimental delivery conformance cannot substitute for quality evidence. Thus public promotion is not a circular prerequisite for gathering its own evidence.
- sr-roadmap-l1i.7.2 and .7.11 separate local renderer verification/P6 shadow acceptance from the later actual experimental advisory trial. P6 does not wait on P7 trial evidence to finish its own shadow boundary.

### Fail-open hook and safe installation: requirements present, execution unproved

.7.1/.7.2/.7.11 classify the dedicated hook before non-exiting parsing and require empty stdout, sanitized stderr and exit zero for pre-publication failures, never blocking fields. Partial publication is separately classified as unknown delivery without retry/replacement JSON, not falsely promised empty output. .7.2 requires a current-mode final check. .7.3 limits writes/removal to the managed entry, uses trusted absolute executable paths, private backups and cooperating locks, preserves permissions, detects conflicts and explicitly disclaims compare-and-swap safety against unrelated external writers. Timeout changes cannot exceed the installed outer budget silently. .7.9 requires independent consent and explicit ledger initialization for recorded trials, not implicit installer activation.

### Independence and empirical gates: requirements present, studies unproved

.8.1 preserves at least 300 independent-family primary relevance cases, positive/no-match/near-miss and overflow coverage requirements, separate explicit-resolution metrics and frozen uncertainty methods. .8.2/.8.3 use equivalent isolated paired tasks with blinded review and family-level harm-or-unresolved endpoints; repeated runs do not enlarge independent sample size. Zero of 100 fails the 2% harm bound; zero of 150 meets it only under the declared valid model. Missing/unjudgeable outcomes are not silently dropped. The controlled harm cohort is distinct from the relevance holdout. .8.4 includes outages/timeouts across at least 500 representative invocations; .8.5 requires actual manual observations and disallows adoption-as-usefulness or unmatched cost claims.

### Release and TUI boundaries

No assigned record promises a GitHub Actions path. .8.7 names DSR exclusively in its goal and explicitly forbids GitHub Actions fallback in both focused verification and AC text. Other standard evidence sections name DSR as the sole release orchestrator; .8.9/.8.10 make no release promise. This matches the supplied prohibition and the targeted AGENTS.md release-rule excerpt. References to TUI in .7.8/.7.10/.7.11/.7.12/.7.13 and the P7 promotion/layout material retain it as later P9 work with its own behavioral gate; they do not require shipping TUI to accept P6.
